projects.name: MapTrace
projects.question: Teaching models to read maps
projects.alt: MapTrace example: a requested route traced across a synthetic zoo map.
projects.summary: Multimodal models can recognize a map yet struggle to follow a route. MapTrace generates synthetic maps and route annotations to train this spatial skill.
projects.detail: Public release: two million annotated map–path examples.

projects.name: X-InstructBLIP
projects.question: Connecting images, audio, video, and 3D to language models
projects.alt: X-InstructBLIP architecture connecting image, audio, video, and 3D encoders to a frozen language model.
projects.summary: A framework for connecting image, audio, video, and 3D inputs to a frozen language model. Independently trained modality adapters support reasoning across multiple input types.
projects.detail: Evaluated across 16 benchmarks; includes generated instruction data and the DisCRn benchmark.

related.name: Contra4
related.summary: A benchmark for contrastive reasoning across up to four modalities.

projects.name: ViUniT
projects.question: Testing the reasoning behind an answer
projects.alt: ViUniT example showing how visual unit tests expose a program that produces a correct answer for the wrong reason.
projects.summary: Visual programs can produce the right answer with faulty logic. ViUniT generates image–answer test cases to check that logic and uses the results for program selection, repair, and learning.
projects.detail: Average accuracy gains of 11.4 percentage points across three datasets in the paper’s visual-programming experiments.

projects.name: Interactive Visual Gym
projects.question: Evaluating assistants in interactive worlds
projects.alt: Interactive Visual Gym task sequences in simulated cooking, household, and mobile-interface environments.
projects.summary: An assistant’s advice changes what a user does next. Interactive Visual Gym simulates users and task environments so models can be evaluated and trained through the consequences of their guidance.
projects.detail: Cooking, household tasks, and mobile interfaces; 315 benchmark interaction scenarios.
